doc: DEGENERATE: a size field of 2.0 (a cell larger than the tile) accepts exactly one point, so the k=2 query has no second neighbor: scipy returns distance inf (and index n), border = inf everywhere and s_cell is that point's size. Never reached by the generator (sizes are at most 0.2); pins the cKDTree k > n semantics (inf, not an error). The output holds infinities (equal to themselves in the check). Draws in call order: plan0 = the Poisson candidates and keep mask of poisson_points(size_field, seed) (default spacing 0.85; the thinning that produced the keep mask from uniforms is pinned by the poisson.* cases, input thin_u), plan1 and plan2 = the white noise of the two warp fBms (low 3, slope 3, seeds seed + 1 and seed + 2); the warp is BORDER_WARP (0.12) x the local size x the fBm, added to the texel center and wrapped with np.mod(., 1.0); the 2 nearest points come from a periodic KD tree (boxsize 1). Outputs: border = (F2 - F1) / size of the nearest cell; s_cell = the size of the nearest cell, a COPY of a size_field value (a port that is handed size_field copies it: bit-exact; it is compared at 1e-12 relative only because the Python check recomputes size_field with the local FFT, which may differ by an ulp from the frozen one); and the accepted Poisson points, an intermediate (exact: copies of the drawn candidates). Measured: every random input nudged by one float64 ulp (8 trials) and numpy.fft replaced by scipy.fft: border max |diff| 8.6e-15 (F2 - F1 cancels), s_cell unchanged in every trial (the nearest cell never flipped), so border rtol 1e-9 / atol 1e-10, s_cell rtol 1e-12.
